notes: All twelve images were read as pixels. The shell is consistent across th/en and light/dark: the sidebar names the product (โยงกิจ/Yongkit), the header names the organisation, the warehouse sits in the sidebar when expanded and moves into the header's second line on the rail and on phones, and the language button shows the target language in its own script with a hidden 'switch to' prefix. Thai labels show no clipped tone marks or vowels in the drawer, sidebar, rail header or page header. The main cross-screen issue is the selected-row treatment: the current page uses the same 1px outline as the warehouse select and the search trigger (sidebarRow.ts:15, SearchTriggers.tsx:100), which flattens the hierarchy in the drawer, the expanded sidebar and most visibly the rail; filed on shell-drawer and shell-rail. Minor inconsistency not filed as a finding: in both drawer captures the account avatar is a flat grey circle while the desktop sidebar shows the purple Clerk avatar, which looks like the avatar image had not loaded in the drawer portal at capture time. The phone header truncates the organisation name earlier in Thai ('Industrial SAS Loc…') than in English because 'English' is wider than 'ไทย'; this involves the seeded name (D8) and has a title attribute, so it is not filed. The search dialog itself is not in this image group and was not judged here.

All 12 images were read as pixels. Both screens are clean on axe with no page overflow; Thai wraps by word (for example 'เมื่อเลือก / AI คำค้น…' in the AI disclosure) with no clipped tone marks in rows, headings or the input. Query matches are highlighted in names, codes and aliases (Linear pattern met). The AI entry follows D14/D16 in every capture: an examples group before typing and a labelled row after the typed results, with the disclosure. Phone rows are 48 px (min-h-touch); desktop uses the dense 36 px rows and shows a keyboard hint that switches from 'Esc to close' to 'Esc to clear' once text is typed. Dark mode uses a neutral grey selected row while light mode uses the accent tint; both keep the 3 px left accent bar, so selection does not rely on colour fill alone. Cross-screen: the employee result layout (three lines, link-coloured action) is the main density cost and shows most on search-results--mixed.

All 12 images were read as pixels. Search no-match is the strongest screen: the preselected AI row (D14/D16 copy present in both locales, no clipping of Thai marks at 390 px), the Go-to fallback list with module labels on the right, ~48 CSS px phone rows, and a desktop keyboard footer. Across screens, the AI row has two visual identities (tinted card with sparkle when offered, plain spinner row when running); unify them on the ASK option styling. In the running capture the query 'pallets of DEMO-DRINK' is a warehouse question while the AI scope sentence lists only time, leave, requests and employees; per D13 this is not scored down, but the product owner may want the typed AI row to say up front when the query is outside AI scope (behaviour, not filed). Shell loading keeps the page layout (title, card, skeleton) and names what is happening with a Reload action and an auto-retry sentence in natural Thai; light-mode skeleton bars are very faint against white, which matters little because the card text names the state. The English phone header truncation is the only text cut seen in this group; Thai strings fit at both widths.

I read all ten images as pixels: not-found th mobile light, th desktop light, en mobile dark, en desktop dark; route-error th mobile light, th desktop light, en mobile dark, en desktop dark, copied th mobile light, retrying en desktop dark. Cross-screen: both pages use the same Button variants (48 px on phone, 36 px dense on desktop), the same h1 scale and the same muted body text, and Thai and English carry the same meaning. Thai tone marks and above/below vowels are not clipped in the h1s, the Notice, the buttons or the reference chip ("ครั้ง", "ชั่วคราว", "ผู้ดูแล"). Dates follow the locale: "5 พ.ย. 2569 20:30" in Thai, "Nov 5, 2026, 8:30 PM" in English. Neither page overflows at 390 px, and axe is clean on every capture. Not-found renders outside the signed-in shell with the neutral "ไปหน้าเริ่มต้น / Go to start page" action, as D11 requires, so it has no search or sidebar; the in-shell route error keeps the header search on phone and the ⌘K sidebar search on desktop. On the phone not-found, Thai wraps "อีกครั้ง" as "อีก / ครั้ง" (a legal word break, though an awkward one); I did not file this as a finding because the screen has a P2. Every retry generates a new reference code, so a member who noted the first code before retrying will hold a different code from the one now shown. The copied line contains both, but the UI does not say so; this belongs under the retrying finding. The benchmark section covers global search, and no benchmark product targets 404 or route-error pages, so bestReference is empty for both screens.
